Subject: MAP: capacity runway & staggered GPU delivery for Elysium pilot -> prod

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Per our request, attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on capacity reservation and the evaluation cadence for the pilot -> production ramp. High level ask: we want to align on lead times for Dedicated vs Private deployments and an initial GPU pool sizing that allows the pilot to be representative of prod latency/cost.

Quick summary of the proposed MAP items:
- Pilot (6 weeks): reserve a small Dedicated pool for evaluation — recommend 8x A100-80GB equivalent pooled GPUs (continuous batching enabled).
- Staggered prod ramp (12 weeks): expand to 32x A100-equivalent in two phases (week 1–6 add 12 GPUs, week 7–12 add remaining 12).
- Lead times: Dedicated GPU pool provisioning: 6–8 weeks from signed reservation. Private (VPC/on‑prem) packaging & procurement: 10–12 weeks (longer where on‑prem procurement is required).
- Fallback: Hosted API burst for peak traffic during the ramp if capacity commit lags.

Action items for this thread (proposed):
1) Elysium: confirm pilot target start (w/c Jun 28) and acceptance criteria for model quality/latency.
2) Procurement: confirm PO timeline or internal approval steps; include any preferred vendor constraints.
3) Redwood: share finalized GPU sizing recommendations and procurement spec (attached GPU-POC-specs.pdf).

I've attached the MAP spreadsheet (Elysium-MAP-v2.xlsx) with milestones and dates so we can slot these into your procurement and engineering calendars.

If you want to adjust the numbers/tempo I can coordinate with Laura and Dev on alternate phasing.

Best,

Subject: RE: MAP capacity sizing notes for Elysium (internal)

Dylan / Dev — internal note on sizing and lead-time tradeoffs before we finalize the MAP to send externally: 

- Pilot realism: 8x A100-80GB gives representative KV cache hit behavior and warm KV cache sizing; 4 GPUs will under-index queuing behavior at p50/p95 when concurrency > 4. If Elysium's acceptance criteria focus on latency under concurrency, keep 8 for pilot. If they're purely model-quality focused, 4 may suffice.
- Ded vs Private procurement: Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pool) is quicker—6 weeks typical if no special compliance addenda. Private (customer VPC or on‑prem) requires infra packaging, networking runbook, and KMS integration — plan for 10–12 weeks.
- Staggered pool approach: recommend 3-phase commit to reduce financial burden: 8 (pilot) -> +12 (initial prod tranche) -> +12 (full prod). Tie KPls and spend checkpoints at each tranche.
- Risk mitigation: include auto-fallback rules in MAP: route 10–20% of traffic to hosted API during initial prod expansion; include SLA credit note in case of provisioning slip.

I've attached a condensed spec we can hand to procurement (GPU-POC-specs.pdf).

Laura

Emily / Procurement / Carlos —

Per internal sizing notes (cc'd Laura and Dev), here's an updated MAP with concrete asks and timelines so procurement has clear line items: 

Proposed commitments and line items:
- Pilot (6 weeks): Reserved Dedicated pool — 8 x A100-80GB equivalent (continuous-batching optimized). Target pilot start: week of Jun 28.
- Phase 1 (weeks 1–6 of prod ramp): add 12 x A100-equivalent (total 20).
- Phase 2 (weeks 7–12): add remaining 12 (total 32).
- Dedicated provisioning lead time: 6 weeks from signed reservation + PO clearance.
- Private on‑prem/VPC install: 10–12 weeks accounting for networking/KMS and customer change control.

Procurement line items (suggested language):
1) "Redwood Dedicated Reserved Capacity — 8 A100-80GB equivalent GPUs — 6 week delivery window — MLP Pilot"
2) "Redwood Dedicated Reserved Capacity — 12 A100-80GB equivalent GPUs — delivery window aligned with Phase 1"
3) "Optional Private Deployment Package — on‑prem/VPC install, network runbook, KMS integration — 10–12 week delivery"

Fallback & acceptance: if Dedicated provisioning slips beyond 10 business days past planned date, Redwood will enable Hosted API bursting up to 20% traffic to cover peak; acceptance criteria for each tranche: p50 & p95 latency targets (see MAP spreadsheet), model perplexity/quality checklists, and infra readiness signoff.

Next steps: 
- Emily: confirm acceptance criteria and pilot start date (can you confirm Jun 28?).
- Procurement / Carlos: confirm PO cadence and whether the procurement team needs any vendor-specific fields (tax id, address, SOW reference).
- Redwood: we'll update MAP spreadsheet after you confirm acceptance criteria.

Thanks — looking forward to closing timelines.

Dylan
